**Key negatives (all cited in the file)**
- **Recall hook:** fired 0/207 on real prompts, and its bench result (−0.008, CI [−0.042, +0.017]) was noise, so the source says not to rely on it (hooks/README.md:28, 31-32, 37-38).
- **Hebbian vs Thompson:** a tie, 0.7239 vs 0.7234 success with slightly worse regret (hebbian-router README:326-330). The no-decay mesh.rs-style rule scored 0.518. Pheromone used as a selector scored 0.25, below random, and the "biological" mechanisms all hurt.
- **Rejected token levers in neural-mesh:**
  - query-adaptive k (RD-LOG:299) and the marginal-return k rule (:337)
  - length-aware re-rank (:320) and the BM25-confidence encoder skip (:356)
  - tool routing saves ~0 tokens on agent delegation (:332)
  - exact-match memo hit rate .14, and 0.000 on delegation prompts (:334)
  - local-LLM front end: 23.5% of local answers wrong against a 10% target (:423-424); fine-tuned local model win rate .438 (llm/README:39)
  - embedding kNN router .449 vs a hand-written phase-verb rule at .913 (:415)
  - discounted-UCB leader (:417); cosine near-duplicate detection (dedup.rs:5-6)
- **Over-trimming:** name-only catalog lines lose about 4.7 points of selection accuracy.
- **Measurement cost:** each measurement subagent paid the ~95k spawn prefix, so an experiment can cost more tokens than it saves (RD-LOG:362).

**Main design implication:** the biggest measured token lever is the spawn prefix (dispatching to lean agents, entries 1 and 6), not retrieval or prompt text. For routing, which learner you pick matters little. The useful parts are learning from outcomes and feeding clean signals: environment-vs-skill failure labels and supervised labels.
